title: Middle Reformed view (most common): faith in both faculties as aggregate
source_text: XII. Porro inter duas istas sententias, quae in hoc negotio videri possunt extremae, & quasi e regione oppositae, est tertia quaedam media, quae in Schola Reformata longe communior est. Illa est quae statuit fidem justificantem, nec in solo intellectu, nec in sola voluntate esse, sed utrique facultati proprie, formaliter, & subjective inesse. Et hoc quia constat actibus partim ab intellectu, partim a voluntate ortis & elicitis. Nec enim est unus simplex habitus, vel actus, sed aggregatum plurium actuum, vel habituum.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover between those two opinions, which in this business can seem extremes and as if regionally opposed, there is a certain third middle view, far more common in the Reformed school. It is the one that holds justifying faith is neither in intellect alone nor in will alone, but inheres in both faculties properly, formally, and subjectively. And this because it consists of acts arisen and elicited partly from intellect, partly from will. For it is not one simple habit or act, but an aggregate of several acts or habits.
pass_b_english: Most Reformed take a middle: justifying faith formally in both intellect and will.
Not one simple habit — an aggregate of intellect- and will-elicited acts.

choices.why: Inheres as in a subject in both faculties.
